symptom: `describe microflow` of a graph whose branches cross INSIDE another branch gives MDL that `mxcli check` rejects and that is not the stored flow. Evora Factory Management: SnowflakeIntegration/SnowflakeRESTSQL.Request_Validation end in `merge shared1; join shared2;` after every branch has returned, with nothing declaring shared2 (MDL-FLOW02, MDL003); AgentCommons.Tool_Validate prints its one stored `call microflow MicroflowSelection_GetCreate` twice (MDL063) and its section fails with "variable 'IsValid' is not declared"
cause: Mode 2 labels a crossed merge, and traverseFlow / traverseFlowUntilMerge / continueAfterSplitJoin `join` it on arrival — but five other places walk THROUGH a merge without asking: continueAfterNestedSplitJoin, the split-type continuation at both levels, and the guard-clause false-branch skip at both levels. Walked through, the crossed merge's suffix was printed inline; then either the walk marked it visited, so emitCrossedMergeSections never declared it and the other branches' joins dangled (Snowflake), or the walk ran on an arm's private visited copy (case / split type arms use cloneVisited), so the section printed the suffix a second time (Tool_Validate). Separately, the check-time validator scoped variables by text order, so a section placed after the `split type` arm that declares $IsValid could not see it
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_show_helpers.go` (joinCrossedMerge / isLabelledMerge at every merge pass-through), `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_validate.go` (recordJoinScope / enterMergeScope: a `merge` sees what its joins declared), `mdl/executor/validate_microflow.go` (MDL005 stops at a `merge`); invariant helper `mdl/executor/describe_graph_invariant_test.go` (assertDescriptionRebuildsGraph); tests in `cmd_microflows_describe_irreducible_test.go`, `validate_merge_scope_test.go`; repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/describe-irreducible-crossed-merge-in-branch.mdl`
insight: **A crossed label is only as good as its least careful walker.** Grep for every `visited[<merge>] = true` followed by a walk of `flowsByOrigin[<merge>]` — each is a pass-through that must ask isCrossed first; there were five, and one rule fixes all of them. **Prove a description by rebuilding it**, not by reading it: assertDescriptionRebuildsGraph parses the description, builds it with the real builder and compares the graph modulo exclusive merges (objects keyed by kind + @position, so a duplicate shows as two rebuilt objects on one stored position). Run over all 1,877 Evora flows it is a sweep, not a spot check. And know what `Unchanged` means for `create or modify` of a describe output: it is the splice verdict — the script's AST equals the stored flow's OWN description — so it proves the output parses, checks and is deterministic, NOT that it is the stored graph; the rebuild comparison is the proof
